title: Mini quant + prompt run cheatsheet
content:
2026-03-25 / quick personal runbook

Purpose: fast scratchpad for small quantization + prompt-sensitivity experiments that I want to spin up, capture immediate observations, and then iterate from. Not a polished report — just enough context to reproduce or escalate.

---
High-level objective
- Find a quantization profile that reduces VRAM by ~40–60% vs FP16 but keeps generation quality within ~3–5% of baseline on our small eval set (conversational + instruction prompts).
- Measure KV-cache warmup + cold-start latency impact for short-latency (<200ms token) usecases.

Quick runs (IDs are local, ephemeral)
- QN-260325-01 (baseline)
  - model: redwood-open-7b-v2 (fp16 weights)
  - config: sequence=1024, batch=1, no quant, kv-cache enabled
  - metrics: avg token-latency=36ms, mem=10.8GB, avg BLEU-ish proxy=0.87 (high-level), human-smoke-check: good
  - notes: stable; used as reference for quality comparisons

- QN-260325-02 (q8_0)
  - model: same weights -> q8_0 (symmetric per-tensor) via inhouse convert script (toolchain v0.9.2)
  - config: seq=1024, batch=1, kv-cache enabled
  - metrics: avg token-latency=32ms, mem=7.2GB, proxy=0.84 (drop ~3.5%)
  - notes: small quality drop for arithmetic/precise numeric answers, otherwise OK; latency improved ~11%

- QN-260325-03 (q4_gptq)
  - model: GPTQ 4-bit per-channel (group size=32), reorder=true, act-order preserved
  - config: seq=1024, batch=1, kv-cache ON
  - metrics: avg token-latency=39ms, mem=4.9GB, proxy=0.78 (drop ~10%)
  - notes: memory good, but tail-case hallucination rate up. Need to test with reranking or ensemble. KV cache interaction: first few tokens slower due to dequant overhead; steady-state token step slightly faster than fp16 but overall gen time higher for short sequences.

- QN-260325-04 (q4+kv-cache-hint)
  - same as QN-03 but enabled prefix caching and prefetch for first 8 tokens
  - metrics: avg token-latency=34ms, mem=5.0GB, proxy=0.80
  - notes: prefetch helped short prompts (<= 40 tokens) — recommended as a mitigation for q4-run dequant cost.

Observational log (free-form)
- Dequant overhead: our runtime currently dequantizes per-block on-the-fly; the cost is proportional to (#layers * group ops). For q4_gptq group=32 the hot-path cost ~ +6ms/token on my local bench.
- KV-cache hit-rate: naive tests show 0.62 hit-rate for conversational reuse patterns (we need synthetic tests that mimic short-turns). When prefetching first 8 tokens into the cache we see effective hit-rate -> 0.84 and latency drops for token 9+.
- Quant quality failure modes: numeric fidelity, list comprehension, and few-shot chain-of-thought degrade fastest. Prompts with explicit example chains (3 shots) are more brittle under q4.

Prompt set (short list used for smoke eval)
- P1 (instruction): "Summarize the following paragraph in 2 sentences: {input}"
- P2 (qa): "Answer concisely: {question} -- If unsure, say 'I don't know.'"
- P3 (few-shot cot): 3-shot chain-of-thought for reasoning tasks (used to stress test): [ex1], [ex2], [ex3], "Now solve: {problem}"
- P4 (dialog): system: "You are a helpful assistant." user: "{turn1}\n{turn2}\nPlease continue the conversation in one paragraph."

Quick reproduction commands (local)
- convert: ./scripts/convert_weights.sh --model redwood-open-7b-v2 --mode gptq --groupsize 32 --out /tmp/qn-03
- bench: python infra/bench_gen.py --model /tmp/qn-03 --seq 1024 --batch 1 --kv-cache --warm 8 --out results/qn-03.json
- smoke eval (prompts): python eval/smoke.py --model /tmp/qn-03 --prompts prompts/mini.json --metrics rouge,exact-match --out smoke/qn-03

Immediate to-dos (priority order)
1) Run synthetic short-turn microbench with prefetch toggles (Kofi to help instrument). deadline: 2026-03-27
2) Create a minimal reranker test that reorders top-4 candidates with fp16 scoring. If q4 causes hallucination we might hide risky outputs behind reranking. (Mira)
3) Add a small few-shot suite focusing on numeric fidelity + list outputs (10 prompts). Quick labels by eyeballing.
4) Try alternate GPTQ group sizes: 16 vs 64 and record per-token CPU overhead.

Notes to self / heuristics
- If mem reduction needed more than 60% try q2_0 only after measuring catastrophic quality loss — probably not useful for customer-facing chat.
- For >1.5x throughput targets consider mixing q8 for embedding/encoder-ish parts and q4 for LM core if pipeline supports it (experimental).
- Prefetch-first-n=8 is a cheap win for short-turn flows; consider exposing as a routing policy for latency-sensitive routes.

Open questions (to triage)
- Is there a cheap metric that correlates with hallucination risk under quantization? (per-token entropy? unusual token distribution?)
- Can we precompute dequantized kernels for the first k layers to avoid per-request overhead? Memory tradeoff vs latency?

Slack / links / references
- Slack thread: #aml-quant (search: "q4 prefetch test 03/25")
- Internal note: confluence/internal/quant-profiles (WIP)

End-of-day micro-retro (26 Mar)
- Wins: q8_0 looks promising as a near-drop-in for many prompts; big mem savings with small quality loss.
- Risks: q4 requires more mitigation layers (prefetch, rerank).
- Next focus: automate short-turn microbench to produce graphs (latency vs prompt-length vs profile) so we can present to product for tradeoff decisions.

---
Small appendix (copyable snippet)
- bench run collector (bash):
  for r in qn-*; do jq '.summary' results/$r.json >> master-summary.json; done

- quick remind: when filing ENG-1298 include: workload trace id, warm/cold ratios, and prompt set name.
